summary_en: This study tests ligufalimab (AK117) given together with cadonilimab (AK104) in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer) and biliary tract cancer that has failed prior therapy. Both drugs are given by intravenous infusion in the clinic on day 1 of every 21-day cycle, with ligufalimab infused over 120 minutes and cadonilimab over 60 minutes, starting at least 30 minutes after ligufalimab. Treatment continues if evaluations show the disease has not gotten worse, and the main outcome measure is not stated; this is a Phase 2 study.
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa ligufalimab (AK117) administrado junto con cadonilimab (AK104) en cáncer de hígado avanzado (carcinoma hepatocelular) y cáncer de vías biliares que ha fracasado a tratamientos previos. Ambos medicamentos se administran por infusión intravenosa en la clínica el día 1 de cada ciclo de 21 días, con ligufalimab durante 120 minutos y cadonilimab durante 60 minutos, iniciando al menos 30 minutos después de ligufalimab. El tratamiento continúa si las evaluaciones muestran que la enfermedad no ha empeorado, y la medida de resultado principal no está indicada; es un estudio de fase 2.
who_for: Advanced or metastatic liver or biliary cancer not suitable for surgery or local therapy, or progressed after these treatments.
Disease that is refractory to or has relapsed after prior anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 antibody therapy.
At least one measurable lesion of at least 1 cm on contrast imaging.
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance score of 0 to 1.
Adequate blood counts, organ function and albumin; Child-Pugh A or B7 for the liver cancer cohort.
not_for: Prior liver transplant or other solid-organ transplant.
Stopped prior immune checkpoint inhibitor due to Grade 4 toxicity, or due to Grade 2 or higher serious immune-related toxicity.
Active autoimmune disease or autoimmune disease needing systemic treatment in the past 2 years.
Known active tuberculosis, known HIV positive status, or pregnancy or breastfeeding.
Symptomatic or clinically active brain metastases, leptomeningeal disease, or carcinomatous meningitis.
